title: A longitudinal analysis of employment in people with severe mental illnesses in India
cohort_overlap_notes: DISTINCT from pune_public (khare2022 / unknown2022). khare2021 recruited at two PRIVATE hospitals, Poona Hospital and Research Centre in Pune (urban) and Manasdeep Psychiatric and Addiction Treatment Center in Ahmednagar (rural), n=550 at baseline and 456 analysed at 12 months (Methods 2.1, p. 473). pune_public is a public-sector psychiatric services sample of 107. No participant overlap is possible: different hospitals, different sectors, different sample sizes. The baseline report of this same cohort is Khare et al. 2020, cited throughout but not staged in this batch.
notes: VERIFIED 287/456 in any paid work at the 12-month follow-up, derived by summing two printed, mutually exclusive and exhaustive cells (257 working at both assessments + 30 not working at baseline but employed at follow-up). See extraction_outcomes.csv.

title: Development and validation of multivariable prediction models of remission, recovery, and quality of life outcomes in people with first episode psychosis: a machine learning approach
cohort_overlap_notes: Contributes results for its DEVELOPMENT cohort national_eden only. It also reports figures for three EXTERNAL VALIDATION samples that belong to other reports and must not be pooled from here: (1) opus_1998, already extracted as hansen2024 and hansen2024b; (2) crisp_glasgow and (3) glasgow_edinburgh_2006, both reported separately by leighton2019b. leighton2019 pools (2) and (3) into one 'Scottish' figure of 59/142, which is arithmetically identical to leighton2019b's two separately printed cohorts (32/75 + 27/67 = 59/142). All three are recorded as relationship=validation_sample with contributes_results=no.
notes: SEPARATE PUBLICATION from leighton2019b: different journal (Lancet Digital Health v PLOS ONE), different DOI, different author list, different development cohort. Not a staging duplicate. Result extracted: 436/807 EET at 12 months in national_eden, a paid_or_education_or_training composite, not paid_any.

title: Predicting one-year outcome in first episode psychosis using machine learning
cohort_overlap_notes: Describes TWO independently recruited cohorts, so it takes two cohort_ids under D12.5 and codebook rule 11: crisp_glasgow (CR:ISP, n=83, NHS Greater Glasgow & Clyde, 2011-14, the training dataset) and glasgow_edinburgh_2006 (n=79, NHS Glasgow and NHS Edinburgh, 1 Sep 2006 to 31 Aug 2009, the validation dataset). The same participants appear inside leighton2019's pooled 'Scottish' validation sample of 162; leighton2019b is the report of record for both.
notes: SEPARATE PUBLICATION from leighton2019, cited by it as reference 9. Table 1 (p. 6) reports the two cohorts SEPARATELY (32/75 and 27/67), so the manifest note 'two cohorts pooled in one report' is half right: there are two cohorts, but it is leighton2019, not this report, that pools them.

title: Effectiveness of an Assertive Community Treatment program for people with severe schizophrenia in mainland China - a 12-month randomized controlled trial
notes: NEAR-ZERO CELL CONFIRMED as printed: 10/30 ACT v 1/28 control. Recorded exactly as printed with no continuity correction. TWO CORRECTIONS to the triage note: (a) the ascertainment is any_time_during_followup, not point prevalence, because the counts are of patients who 'returned to wage-earning employment ... over the 12-month follow-up'; (b) 'selected for severe impairment' is not an employment-related criterion under D9, so employment selection is coded unclear on incomplete reporting, not selected. Allocated arms only: no whole-cohort row, because the ACT team included a part-time employment specialist and worked on 'setting goals for employment', so employment_targeted_intervention would be yes.
